item.title: Unbearable Hope
item.content:encoded:
“The worst part of holding the memories is not the pain. It's the loneliness of it. Memories need to be shared.”

- Lois Lowry, The Giver

So we step into Nadox for a time and catch a glimpse of the unbearable loneliness he's endured in order to perfect his niŋä's1 Great Plan. Through that, we also must wonder what Ion themself endured.

Many thanks to DrAkimoto, for his critique and support throughout this project. Without it, I doubt Memoria would ever even exist. Unlike Nadox, I know that I am not doing this alone.

Critters: DrAkimoto, cybersqyd, Grigori Karpin, RockTeethMothEyes, & OriCat. Thank you all, you are also instrumental to making this work.

item.title: SCP-5217
item.content:encoded:
I had this idea in July when I read SCP-1423 and saw a photo a former classmate posted on the same day (not the one in the article, for licensing reasons). It just wouldn't get out of my head, so I decided to flesh it out fully, then to work to make it unique, then to put it in Wikidot format in a sandbox. Figured I might as well cold-post it and see if it sinks or swims.

I don't know if this story continues or not, but if it does, I'm sure that it happens in the Academics version of War on All Fronts. But this won't even survive 24 hours so it's pretty silly to think that'll happen.

Lots of people to thank, first among them my friend Alice for drawing the sketch at the end. Next up is RJB_R for writing the SCP that inspired this, even if it has evolved quite a bit since then. Then qntm, who gets a shoutout through Site 41 in the article, for being so dang cool. Also thanks to the people who made the Wiki Syntax guide (I stole all your code no regrets!) and the people who wrote the How to Write an SCP guide for saying that sentient beings have to be Euclid and Foundation personnel aren't stupid. Breaking rules is fun if you're clever about it and don't care about the result!

Have a great day and a great life, and if you upvote, a good month as well!

item.title: SCP-5923
item.content:encoded:
This is the second article I wrote after The 13 Correlation, which I'll admit suffers from some first-article frays. This has memetic infiltration, pro career cover-ups, cosmic invasion/apocalypse catalyst, auto-creation of reality through observer effects, a play by play of a rapid Big Rip in the Foundation-verse, how it'd interact with various physical anomalies, a precision redaction about one of my favorite early SCPs that seems creepy in a mystical way.

And to top it off, a spook. I didn't expect to find a face in a quasar.

I think I'm hitting a lot of SCP-genre keynotes here while also bringing some fresh spin. I hope you agree.

item.title: SCP-5134
item.content:encoded:
The classic first SCP downvote guantlet. Hope this makes it. Please excuse any perceived impudence for not pipelining work from a new account through the greenlighting and draft review, I have 11 finished articles produced in the last week and figured it'd be better to let things face Darwinian pressure.

The hypermodern themes of informatic SCPs embedded in the corners of our digital reality is something I'm generally interested in so even if this *didn't* land with you, I'm very interested in discussing those themes.

item.title: SCP-5233
item.content:encoded:
Big big big thanks to my lovely reviewers in chat: Pratten, Savan, Calibri_Bold, Mars, chaucer345, and Karakatt for all your wonderful suggestions to better develop the backstory here!

Image source is here: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_earwig_(Forficula_auricularia)_on_thumb.jpg

Notes:
- All of Wiggy’s interview excerpt dialogue consists of words found in the Wikipedia article for Earwig: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earwig
- Why earwigs? 1. When I was in elementary school, my friends and I found a very large pincher bug on the playground and admired it. Some other kid picked it up and tore off its pincers to keep as a souvenir. That image has stuck with me for over a decade. I can’t smush earwigs anymore. Also last month I found one in a box at work the other day and I let him go outside and it reminded me of that incident. 2. Quoth Wikipedia, “Earwigs are among the few non-social insect species that show maternal care.” Pinchy pinch moms are good moms. There’s a lot of neat facts about earwigs.
- Why Arizona? During my background research, I found this: https://cals.arizona.edu/yavapai/anr/hort/byg/archive/earwig.html so I just went with Arizona.

Best wishes to everyone in this crazy year. To everyone who has the opportunity to nurture a life, no matter how small, and those who teach others to do the same, you are the hope of the world.
